methods.name: AdaBoost.M1, SAMME and AdaBoost.R2 with depth-limited CART weak learners
methods.reference: SAMME (Zhu et al. 2009; adabag::boosting(coeflearn = 'Zhu', boos = FALSE)) and AdaBoost.M1 written out in R with rpart::rpart weak learners (adabag not a case dependency); rpart anova for the first R2 learner
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md, n = 120: 1e-8 relative; labels and accuracies exact

methods.name: XGBoost exact and histogram trees: L1 leaf weights and gains
methods.reference: xgboost::xgb.train(tree_method = 'exact') 3.2 for the exact trees (case ml_xgboost_pkg); XGBoost exact greedy (Chen & Guestrin 2016) and p2a's histogram variant with xgboost's CalcWeight/CalcGain L1 rule, published algorithm written out in R (ml_xgboost_l1). The package's histogram trees bin differently and are not compared.
quantities: root split feature, threshold and gain
package predictions, root split and gain, alpha 0 and 3
methods.tolerance: validation/README.md, n = 16: 1e-6 relative; split feature and bin exact; the xgboost package: 1e-6 absolute (it computes in single precision)

methods.name: Component-wise boosting with bols learners: Gaussian, Binomial(), Binomial(type = 'glm'), Poisson; least-squares tree learner
methods.reference: mboost::mboost(y ~ bols(x1) + bols(x2) + bols(x3)) 2.9 (case ml_mboost_pkg: offset, coefficients, selections, fitted responses after 100 steps); the same family definitions (R/family.R) written out in R (ml_mboost_bols: also the first step and the 2000-step paths); stats::lm and stats::glm for the limits; the tree learner is p2a's own least-squares tree written out in R, a self-consistency check, not R-pinned (mboost's btree is ctree-based)
methods.tolerance: 100-step paths and tree fits: validation/README.md, n = 200: 1e-8 relative; 2000-step paths and limits: 1e-6 relative (iterative)

methods.name: Probit BART (classification) by data augmentation
methods.reference: BART::pbart model (the BART package is not a dependency of these cases): exact posterior with unsplittable trees by stats::integrate; glm(binomial(probit)) as a property target
quantities: posterior mean and SD of P(y = 1)
methods.tolerance: offset 1e-6 relative; posterior mean 0.009 and SD 0.006 absolute (5 Monte Carlo SDs from 200 R replications); glm property: mean absolute difference < 0.085, correlation > 0.90

deviations.note: Probit and regression BART share a kernel whose Metropolis-Hastings ratio is an open finding (ML-16, ML-121); the single-leaf pin excludes it and the glm property is insensitive to it.
